title: Anchor-free simulation up to a terminal state
statement: Let source and host machines have the same number of work tapes and Boolean tape symbols, and let $\mathrm{emb}$ map source states to host states. Fix a host anchor state and a decidable predicate $\mathrm{stop}$ on source states. Assume no embedded source state is the anchor; every source configuration whose state satisfies $\mathrm{stop}$ is fixed by one source step; and, for every state not satisfying $\mathrm{stop}$ and every input and work-tape reading, the host transition from the embedded state is the source transition with its successor state mapped by $\mathrm{emb}$. If source configuration $c$ reaches configuration $d$ after exactly $T$ steps and $d$ has a state satisfying $\mathrm{stop}$, then there is a time $t\le T$ at which the host run from the state-renamed configuration $c$ equals the state-renamed configuration $d$, and every host configuration from time $0$ through $t$ avoids the anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: Source and host machines have the same number of work tapes and Boolean symbols
State map $\mathrm{emb}$ and host anchor state
No embedded source state equals the anchor
Source step fixes every configuration with a terminal state
Host transition agreement on embedded nonterminal states for every input and work reading
Source run from $c$ at time $T$ equals $d$
